question.worked_solution:
The chain rule in vector form states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t).
$$

First, we need to compute $∇f(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}{e}^{x-y}\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}{e}^{x-y}\,j \\  & ={e}^{x-y}\,i-{e}^{x-y}\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute $x={t}^{2}$ and $y=-t$ into the above to find $∇f(r(t)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & ={e}^{{t}^{2}+t}\,i-{e}^{{t}^{2}+t}\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-t)\,j \\  & =2t\,i-\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =({e}^{{t}^{2}+t}\,i-{e}^{{t}^{2}+t}\,j)\cdot (2t\,i-\,j) \\  & ={e}^{{t}^{2}+t}\cdot 2t+(-{e}^{{t}^{2}+t})\cdot (-1) \\  & =(2t+1){e}^{{t}^{2}+t}.\end{aligned}
$$
